title: Koszul cone homology transitions are pro-zero
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $r\in\mathbb N$, $a:\operatorname{Fin}(r)\to A$, and $I=(a_i)$. Write $K_m$ for the Koszul chain complex on $(a_i^{m+1})$ [def-weil-pbc-koszul-complex], and $S_m$ for $A/I^{m+1}$ in degree zero [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology]. Suppose $\epsilon_m:K_m\to S_m$ has degree-zero component the quotient after the canonical degree-zero exterior identification. Suppose $t_{m,k}:K_k\to K_m$ has degree-$n$ component the $n$th exterior power of $e_i\mapsto a_i^{k-m}e_i$, and let $q_{m,k}:S_k\to S_m$ make these augmentation squares commute after extension to integer cochain complexes. Assume that for every $n>0$ and $m$ there is $k\ge m$ with $H_n(t_{m,k})=0$. Then for every $j\in\mathbb Z$ and $m$ there is $k\ge m$ for which the degree-$j$ homology map of the strict homotopy-cofiber map induced by this square is zero.

proof.text: Use the homotopy-cofiber first projection and left inclusion to identify cycles with cycles in the shifted source wherever the quotient complex has zero term. Naturality of extendHomologyIso transfers the supplied positive chain-homology vanishing to cochain degree j+1. If a mapped cycle is a source boundary d(w), the cone boundary of minus the left inclusion of w is its image under the actual strict cone map. This proves every degree j<-1.

For degree -1, a cone cycle projects to a degree-zero source element whose scalar under zeroEquiv lies in I^(k+1), by the specified augmentation. Each a_i lies in the radical of J_m=(a_i^(m+1)). The finite-generation lemma Ideal.exists_pow_le_of_le_radical_of_fg gives s with I^s<=J_m. Choose k=m+s. The degree-zero diagonal is identity, and the boundary into degree zero has image J_m, by the Finsupp linear-combination range, the degree-one exterior equivalence, and the existing private theorem ExteriorAlgebra.koszulBoundary_zero_quotient_formula imported from Sheaf.RingTheory.KoszulProjectiveResolution. Only this elementary boundary identity is reused, without applying the regular-sequence projective-resolution theorem. Lift the cycle scalar through this boundary and then through the extension isomorphism. Its negative cone inclusion is the required boundary. This works for r=0 and I=0 or I=A.

In degree zero the source term in degree one is zero and the augmentation in degree zero is surjective, so every cone element is a boundary: lift its second component through the augmentation and use the cone left inclusion in degree -1. Positive degrees have zero terms because both extended complexes do. The cycle/opcycle homology API then gives zero homology maps.

lean.statement:
theorem koszul_cone_homology_transition_pro_zero
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (r : ℕ) (a : Fin r → A)
    (ε : ∀ m : ℕ, koszulComplex A r (fun i ↦ a i ^ (m + 1)) ⟶
      (ChainComplex.single₀ (ModuleCat.{u} A)).obj
        (ModuleCat.of A (A ⧸ (Ideal.span (Set.range a)) ^ (m + 1))))
    (t : ∀ m k : ℕ, m ≤ k →
      (koszulComplex A r (fun i ↦ a i ^ (k + 1)) ⟶
        koszulComplex A r (fun i ↦ a i ^ (m + 1))))
    (q : ∀ m k : ℕ, m ≤ k →
      ((ChainComplex.single₀ (ModuleCat.{u} A)).obj
          (ModuleCat.of A (A ⧸ (Ideal.span (Set.range a)) ^ (k + 1))) ⟶
        (ChainComplex.single₀ (ModuleCat.{u} A)).obj
          (ModuleCat.of A (A ⧸ (Ideal.span (Set.range a)) ^ (m + 1)))))
    (hε : ∀ m, (ε m).f 0 = ModuleCat.ofHom
      (((Ideal.span (Set.range a)) ^ (m + 1)).mkQ.comp
        (exteriorPower.zeroEquiv A (Fin r →₀ A)).toLinearMap))
    (ht : ∀ m k h n, (t m k h).f n = ModuleCat.ofHom
      (exteriorPower.map n (Finsupp.linearCombination A
        (fun i ↦ Finsupp.single i (a i ^ (k - m))))))
    (hc : ∀ m k h,
      HomologicalComplex.extendMap (t m k h) ComplexShape.embeddingDownNat ≫
          HomologicalComplex.extendMap (ε m) ComplexShape.embeddingDownNat =
        HomologicalComplex.extendMap (ε k) ComplexShape.embeddingDownNat ≫
          HomologicalComplex.extendMap (q m k h) ComplexShape.embeddingDownNat)
    (hpos : ∀ (n : ℕ), 0 < n → ∀ m : ℕ, ∃ (k : ℕ) (h : m ≤ k),
      HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (t m k h) n = 0) :
    ∀ (j : ℤ) (m : ℕ), ∃ (k : ℕ) (h : m ≤ k),
      HomologicalComplex.homologyMap
        (HomologicalComplex.homotopyCofiber.mapArrowHom
          (HomologicalComplex.extendMap (ε k) ComplexShape.embeddingDownNat)
          (HomologicalComplex.extendMap (ε m) ComplexShape.embeddingDownNat)
          (fun j : ℤ ↦ ⟨j - 1, sub_add_cancel j 1⟩)
          (Arrow.homMk
            (HomologicalComplex.extendMap (t m k h) ComplexShape.embeddingDownNat)
            (HomologicalComplex.extendMap (q m k h) ComplexShape.embeddingDownNat)
            (hc m k h))) j = 0
